fatal_errors: The proposed B or C grain-boundary segregation does not reconstruct the demonstrated Re-addition intervention.
No supporting prior evidence is cited.

The claim that B or C will preserve both 1600 °C performance and irradiation resistance is unsupported; interstitial segregation or precipitation could instead cause strengthening, embrittlement, or microstructural instability.
Irradiation conditions and quantitative outcome metrics are not specified.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the requested room-temperature, high-temperature, and irradiation objectives and gives a testable high-level failure rule, but it is largely generic. The target intervention was equiatomic Re addition to sputtered nanocrystalline NbMoTaW films, which refined grains, increased lattice distortion and excess free volume, and generated amorphous grain-boundary regions that acted as defect sinks and suppressed grain-boundary He-bubble accumulation. The generated proposal instead invokes unspecified B or C segregation and a different, weakly developed mechanism. It predicts no quantitative changes in ductility, high-temperature strength, irradiation hardening, bubble size, or boundary segregation. Its boundaries omit film microstructure and irradiation energy, fluence, temperature, and damage depth. The proposed experiment could screen the idea, but it needs matched compositions and microstructures, verified segregation, explicit 1600 °C metrics, defined irradiation conditions, TEM bubble analysis, and mechanical acceptance thresholds. Without citations or direct evidence that B/C segregation remains stable and beneficial under all three assessments, the alternative is not adequately supported.
